channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Mexican Governor Accused by U.S. of Aiding Drug Cartel Steps Down
item.description: Rubén Rocha Moya stepped down as Sinaloa Governor after US prosecutors accused him of aiding the Sinaloa Cartel. He was accused of taking bribes and providing political support. U. S. prosecutors accused Rubén Rocha Moya of protecting the powerful Sinaloa Cartel in exchange for bribes and political support, setting off a national scandal.

item.title: Thirteen killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, health ministry says
item.description: Thirteen people were killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon. Four women and a child were among the dead. Four women and a child are among the dead, as fighting between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah continues despite a ceasefire.

item.title: Mexican governor indicted by US steps down
item.description: Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha Moya stepped down after being indicted by the US. He was accused of protecting the Sinaloa cartel and taking millions in bribes. Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha Moya has been accused of protecting the powerful Sinaloa cartel and helping it smuggle drugs into the US, allegedly taking in millions of dollars in bribes.

item.title: Norris wins Miami sprint in McLaren one-two
item.description: Lando Norris won the Miami sprint in a McLaren one-two. Norris wins Miami sprint in McLaren one-two.

item.title: Trump tells Congress ceasefire means he does not need their approval for Iran war
item.description: US President Trump claims the Iran ceasefire terminates hostilities, arguing he no longer needs congressional approval for war. This assertion contradicts existing law requiring congressional authorisation for military action. The president writes that hostilities "have terminated" because of the ceasefire, arguing he does not need congressional authorisation.

item.description: Leinster beat Toulon to reach the Champions Cup final. Leinster beat Toulon to reach Champions Cup final.

item.title: Brentford go sixth with win over relegation-threatened West Ham
item.description: Brentford won over relegation-threatened West Ham, moving up to sixth place. The win was a significant boost to Brentford's standings. Brentford go sixth with win over relegation-threatened West Ham.

item.title: Why Ukraine and Israel are arguing over grain
item.description: Ukraine and Israel are disputing over grain cargo ships docked in Haifa, which Kyiv claims is stolen from Russian-occupied Ukraine. Israel says there's a lack of evidence. Cargo ships have docked in Haifa, Israel, carrying grain thought to originate from Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine.

item.title: Bayern score in stoppage time to rescue 3-3 draw against strugglers Heidenheim
item.description: Bayern scored in stoppage time to secure a 3-3 draw against Heidenheim. The match was a close one, with both teams showing strong performance. Bayern score in stoppage time to rescue 3-3 draw against strugglers Heidenheim.

item.title: U.S. to Withdraw 5,000 Troops From Germany. But Thousands Will Remain.
item.description: The US will withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany, but tens of thousands of personnel will remain. The US military presence in Germany extends beyond Europe, with significant implications for global security.

item.title: Mexico’s Sinaloa state governor resigns amid US drug trafficking charges
item.description: Mexico's Sinaloa state governor, Ruben Rocha Moya, resigned amid US charges of shielding a drug cartel. He denied allegations and said he's taking a temporary leave to defend himself. Ruben Rocha Moya again denies allegations he shielded cartel, says taking 'temporary leave' to defend self.

item.title: Fighting reaches outskirts of Ukraine's stronghold Kostiantynivka
item.description: Fighting reached the outskirts of Ukraine's Kostiantynivka, a key stronghold in the country's east. The city is part of a well-fortified area by the Ukrainian military. Kostiantynivka, ​along with other cities, forms a so-called fortress ⁠belt in the country’s east - an area well fortified by the Ukrainian military.

item.title: Lyon into Women's Champions League final with 4-3 aggregate win over Arsenal
item.description: Lyon defeated Arsenal 4-3 on aggregate to reach the Women's Champions League final, securing a spot in the championship match. Lyon into Women's Champions League final with 4-3 aggregate win over Arsenal.

item.title: 'Fully Prepared For American Foolishness': Iran Warns Of Possible Renewed War
item.description: Iran's military officer warned of possible renewed war, stating the country's armed forces are fully prepared. This statement comes amid ongoing tensions between Iran and the US. Iran's military officer said that its armed forces are "fully prepared" if escalation happens.

item.title: Yemen says oil tanker hijacked off Shabwa coast, heads towards Somali waters
item.description: A Yemeni oil tanker was hijacked off the Shabwa coast and is heading towards Somali waters, prompting efforts by the coast guard to track its location and ensure the safety of its crew.

item.description: The US threatened sanctions on shipping firms that pay Iran tolls. President Donald Trump expressed skepticism about Iran's peace proposal. The warning comes as President Donald Trump said he was "not excited" by Iran's latest proposal for a peace deal.

item.title: Ukraine’s Drone War Has Already Rewritten NATO’s Future
item.description: Ukraine's use of drones in its conflict has led to a reevaluation of NATO's future, with Kyiv Post suggesting significant changes to the alliance's strategy and capabilities. Ukraine’s Drone War Has Already Rewritten NATO’s Future Kyiv Post.

item.title: US withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany; Berlin urges stronger European defence
item.description: The US is withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany, prompting Berlin to urge stronger European defence. US withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany; Berlin urges stronger European defence.

item.title: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill seven amid fragile ceasefire
item.description: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon killed seven people despite a fragile ceasefire. Attacks hit villages including Kfar Dajal and Lwaizeh. Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported an airstrike on a car in the village of Kfar Dajal that killed two people, while another hit a home in the village of Lwaizeh killing three.
